_metadata.description: Declarative agent operations: the generic operation runner is the sole spawn path; contracts, bindings, policies, and workflows are authored data with pinned provenance. Added at Phase 9 cutover of the declarative-agent-operations plan.

requirements.title: Operation runner is the sole spawn path
requirements.description: Target-bound domain packages never spawn or continue Agent Manager runs directly and never acquire new direct client imports; every autonomous launch flows through the operation runner (opsrunner/opsbridge) and the engine's agentactivity chokepoint, and the generic substrate contains no mode-name branches.

validation.notes: AST guard: no spawn/continue call in any guarded domain package; the legacy allowlist is empty and must stay empty.
Import guard: only allowlisted infrastructure packages may import the Agent Manager client at all.
Purity guard (also opsbridge/opscatalog twins): the generic substrate never names a shipped mode; selection lives in authored data.

requirements.title: Target capabilities gate operation-target compatibility
requirements.description: Each target kind declares the capabilities it provides; an operation binds to a target only when every required capability is provided, failing closed with an actionable error naming what is missing.

validation.notes: Compatibility fails closed on missing capabilities and unknown target kinds.
Every shipped capability descriptor validates against its schema and the closed vocabulary.
Capabilities make one operation shareable across target kinds by data alone.

requirements.title: Operation contracts are validated, versioned, and fully bound
requirements.description: Every operation is a provider-neutral contract (typed inputs, typed result, closed outcomes, evidence expectations, cancellation/retry semantics) that validates against its schema; the shipped catalog materializes the Go SSOT and every contract has a system-default binding.

validation.notes: The seeded contract SSOT validates schema + semantic rules for every operation.
Every SSOT contract is materialized on disk at its version and carries a system-default binding.
The shipped catalog loads fail-closed: a malformed document aborts the whole load.

requirements.title: Layered binding resolution is deterministic and fail-closed
requirements.description: Binding layers resolve with deterministic precedence (authorized-invocation > backlog-item override > initiative override > system default); a malformed higher-precedence override is a typed error, never a silent fallback, and no binding at all is a typed error.

validation.notes: Layer precedence is deterministic regardless of candidate order.
A malformed override never lets a lower layer win.
An invocation with no binding in scope fails with the typed ErrNoBinding.

requirements.title: Executions pin exact revisions; deleted or incompatible revisions fail closed
requirements.description: Every execution pins the exact content revisions (canonical digests) of the contract, binding, policy, and compiled mode that decided it; a binding to an unregistered mode or a mode that cannot serve the target is a typed error through the same checker production wires. Binding mode_revision labels are advisory; enforcement is digest-based.

validation.notes: A binding to a deleted/unregistered mode revision fails closed at invocation.
Every shipped default binding resolves through the production checker (RevisionExists + ModeCompatible) for its mode's target kind.
Execution provenance carries every pinned revision digest the run was decided by.

requirements.title: Workflow instances persist atomically with optimistic concurrency
requirements.description: Workflow instances commit via compare-and-swap (a concurrent writer conflicts, never clobbers) and atomic writes (no torn state on crash); orphaned execution snapshots are reconciled rather than leaked.

validation.notes: Concurrent workflow writes conflict deterministically instead of silently clobbering.
A workflow file is never observable in a torn/partial state.
RunReconciliation lands orphaned execution snapshots back into their workflows; recovery is data-driven.

requirements.title: Transition policies route to registered deterministic actions only
requirements.description: Outcome routing is authored data: a transition policy may only name registered deterministic actions and registered operations, cannot encode arbitrary execution, and committing a result applies exactly the declared transitions.

validation.notes: The policy vocabulary is closed: arbitrary execution cannot be smuggled into routing data.
A policy naming an unregistered action fails validation (and the catalog load).
Committing an operation result records the outcome and applies the policy's declared transitions.

requirements.title: Outcome classification is honest and abstains when underivable
requirements.description: Round outcomes derive from structured handoffs first (L1), fall back to a declared classifier (L2), and ABSTAIN to operator attention when no honest outcome can be derived — a completion without evidence of progress never advances the workflow.

validation.notes: Structured handoff fields short-circuit classification (L1).
An underivable outcome abstains and parks the round for the operator.
A terminal run without declared progress abstains rather than fabricating success.

requirements.title: Legacy execution history is migrated, readable, and never replayed
requirements.description: The one-shot state migration is COMPLETE (promoted epoch 1, 125/125 staged and promoted, zero quarantined); imported legacy execution snapshots stay readable and clearly labeled, are refused for reproduction, and the migration-status document is served for diagnostics. The migrator itself was deleted after promotion; the evidence doc is the durable record.

validation.notes: Migrated (legacy-import) execution snapshots decode and render with their import provenance.
A legacy import cannot be replayed/reproduced as if it carried full pinned provenance.
The migration-status document (promoted) is served through the diagnostics API.
Durable migration evidence: promoted epoch 1, 125/125, 0 quarantined, rollback rehearsal byte-identical, backups retained.

requirements.title: UI presents the operations workflow model with full parity
requirements.description: The UI reads the canonical workflow projection (legal actions server-authoritative), presents the member-item strategy through the single mapping seam (blank and 'item-level' both present as the strategy; the picker's strategy entry is client-synthesized), and renders operation executions including migrated history.

validation.notes: The single UI seam for the sentinel wire-value policy: blank and 'item-level' present as the strategy; stats buckets are relabeled, never dropped.
The UI service maps the canonical workflow/execution projection from the diagnostics API.
The backlog details panel renders the workflow (or the no-workflow default funnel) with server-authoritative legal actions.
